notes: Accredited driving-academy learner-guide refresh built from what a small school actually has. 8 dash-mount narrated takes: two (07/08) are the SAME four-way-stop junction on two passes so the eight files cover only seven scenarios, hazard-recognition has NO take at all, three (03/04/06) carry a long approach with the manoeuvre only in the last seconds (the roundabout take never reaches the roundabout), and two (03/06) are 720-line pre-upgrade among 1080s so the vertical choice is constrained. 6 road stills across one fog-to-low-sun Saturday: two (01/02) shot into the sun with skies clipped to flat paper so highlight recovery returns nothing while reporting success, two (03/04) windscreen frames with a dashboard reflection and a polariser sky band, one (05) off level, one (06) the best-lit neutral reference. The simplified sign glyphs survive only as a phone photo of a taped wall sheet, ink close to paper in the shadowed corner and the yield glyph an enclosed outline a background knockout fills. The real county warning sign is a retro-reflective face against an equally-bright overcast sky so a one-call knockout bites the top edge and the shadowed post. The printer's 2019 press PDF has a fixed-measure steps frame sized around the shortest 2019 scenario that silently truncates any longer record at trim, and the 2026 copy CSV has step lists from 3 to 11 lines with a roundabout row pointing at a photo filename nobody supplied.

assets.defect_engineered: the printed guide reads as four tidy blocks per page, but the NUMBERED STEPS block is a fixed-measure text frame sized in 2019 around the SHORTEST scenario, with no auto-size, no thread and no overset flag exposed, so any longer 2026 record silently stops rendering at the trim edge with no warning in the merge response; the photograph well and the steps block also sit closer together in the artwork than the generous printed page suggests, and the file carries NO bleed.
assets.content:
LAYOUT SPEC for the academy's 2019 learner-guide press PDF (the printer's file; one scenario per page, to be reverse-engineered downstream into a live merge template).

Document: US Letter PORTRAIT, 8.5 x 11 in (215.9 x 279.4 mm). The 2019 file shipped as a MULTI-PAGE guide, ONE SCENARIO PER PAGE, every page built on the same master page. NO bleed box present (trim = media box, 0 mm bleed). Fonts embedded (the 2019 faces are a generic grotesque-sans title and a transitional-serif body, both to be replaced by the new type system).

WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE PRINTED (four apparent blocks per page):
- Top band: a PHOTOGRAPH WELL, a wide landscape image box holding the scenario's road reference picture, roughly the top 40 percent of the page.
- Under it: the SCENARIO TITLE in a large humanist sans, Signal Green #2E6B4F (e.g. 'Roundabouts').
- Middle: a NUMBERED STEPS block, a single column of numbered instruction lines in Slate Text #2A2E33 on the Route White #F7F7F4 ground.
- Bottom: a short CALL-OUT line, one reassuring sentence, with a Caution Amber #E4A11B rule above it.

HOW IT IS ACTUALLY SET (the reverse-engineering traps):
- The NUMBERED STEPS block is a FIXED-MEASURE text frame whose height was sized in 2019 around the SHORTEST scenario in the old copy (about four short lines). It has NO auto-size, does NOT thread to a second frame, and exposes NO overset flag. A record whose step list is longer than that measure does not push the frame, does not spill and does not report overset anywhere in the merge response: the extra lines simply stop rendering at the trim edge and the page still looks finished.
- The PHOTOGRAPH WELL and the STEPS block sit CLOSER TOGETHER in the actual artwork than the generous printed page implies (the 2019 designer tucked the steps frame up under the image), so the real vertical measure available to the steps is smaller than a glance at the printed guide suggests.
- The TITLE, the STEPS block and the CALL-OUT are three separate text frames; the PHOTOGRAPH WELL is a true graphic frame that a per-row image column can bind into.

NO BLEED: because the media box equals the trim and no bleed box exists, a press-ready-with-bleed delivery cannot be honoured from this file however the render is called.

FIELD LABELS the downstream mapping must resolve (present as content, not visible tokens): SCENARIO_TITLE | STEPS | CALLOUT | PHOTO

Colours: Route White #F7F7F4 ground, Signal Green #2E6B4F scenario title, Slate Text #2A2E33 step lines, Caution Amber #E4A11B call-out rule, Sky Grey #9AA6AE thin page footer.

assets.defect_engineered: eight scenario rows whose numbered step lists are WILDLY UNEVEN, from 3 lines (Hazard recognition) to 11 lines (Left turns across traffic), because two instructors wrote them separately with no measure; and the Roundabouts row names a Photo filename (milepost_roundabout_ref.jpg) that does NOT exist in anything the academy supplied (the real roundabout has to be licensed from Stock). Row order and count define the guide's pages; still_06 is reused across two rows as a real school would.
assets.content:
Scenario Title,Steps,Callout,Photo
Lane changes,"1. Check your interior mirror for what is behind you. 2. Check the door mirror on the side you are moving to. 3. Signal in good time. 4. Take a quick glance over your shoulder to clear the blind spot. 5. Move across smoothly in one steady movement. 6. Cancel the signal and settle into the new lane.","One lane at a time. Never two at once.",milepost_road_still_06.jpg
Right turns,"1. Slow down early and get into the correct position. 2. Signal right in good time. 3. Check your mirrors and the road you are turning into. 4. Take the turn at a speed that lets you stay in your own lane. 5. Straighten up and build speed gently once you are round.","Slow in, steady out.",milepost_road_still_03.jpg
Left turns across traffic,"1. Begin slowing well before the junction. 2. Move to the correct position near the centre line. 3. Signal left across the oncoming lane in good time. 4. Stop at the give-way line if you cannot see a clear gap. 5. Watch the oncoming traffic and judge the gaps, not the cars. 6. Look through the turn to where you want to end up. 7. Check for pedestrians crossing the road you are entering. 8. Wait for a gap you are certain of, not one you are hoping for. 9. When the gap is clear, turn smoothly across the lane. 10. Keep your wheels straight while you wait so a knock will not push you forward. 11. Complete the turn into your own lane and cancel the signal.","When in doubt, wait. A missed gap costs seconds; a wrong one costs more.",milepost_road_still_02.jpg
Roundabouts,"1. Read the signs and road markings on the approach. 2. Slow down early and choose your lane before you arrive. 3. Give way to traffic already on the roundabout, usually from your left. 4. Wait for a gap and enter without stopping if you can. 5. Keep to your lane and follow the markings round. 6. Signal left as you pass the exit before the one you want. 7. Leave the roundabout in your lane and check your mirror.","Look left, take your time, and keep moving when it is clear.",milepost_roundabout_ref.jpg
Parallel parking,"1. Find a space at least a car and a half long. 2. Pull up level with the car in front, about half a metre out. 3. Check your mirrors and blind spot for anything coming. 4. Select reverse and begin backing slowly. 5. When your back wheels are level with the other car's bumper, turn the wheel toward the kerb. 6. Bring the car back at a shallow angle. 7. When the front clears the parked car, straighten the wheel. 8. Reverse gently until you are parallel with the kerb. 9. Adjust forward and back until you are centred in the space.","Slow and small. Let the wheel do the work.",milepost_road_still_05.jpg
Merging,"1. Build your speed along the slip road to match the traffic. 2. Check your mirrors as you go. 3. Look for a gap in the lane you are joining. 4. Signal to show where you are going. 5. Keep glancing between the road ahead and your mirror. 6. Ease into the gap at matching speed. 7. Do not stop on the slip road unless you have to. 8. Cancel your signal and keep a safe distance.","Match the speed, find the gap, ease in.",milepost_road_still_04.jpg
Four-way stops,"1. Come to a full stop at the line, every time. 2. The first vehicle to stop is the first to go. 3. If two of you arrive together, the one on the right goes first. 4. When it is your turn, move off clearly so others know.","Full stop, then first come, first go.",milepost_road_still_01.jpg
Hazard recognition,"1. Keep scanning far ahead, not just the car in front. 2. Ask what could happen next and cover the brake. 3. Slow down before a hazard, not on top of it.","See it early, and you have time.",milepost_road_still_06.jpg
